correctness.rationale: Full orthogonal decomposition into pair-reflection -- states (energy -2), single-petal antisymmetric sectors (m quadratic factors and m(m-2) zero modes), symmetric incidence kernel (m(m-3)/2 energy-2 modes), and incidence image (m-1 and one cubic factors); BB^T=(m-2)I+J. Total degree m(2m+1). The residual 5m modes vanish in normalized counting measure; fixed dimensions yield 1/4,1/2,1/4 limit. A standalone construction of the full integer Hamiltonian exactly matches the claimed characteristic polynomial for all 3<=m<=7. Numerical enumeration is corroborative, not a universal proof. Boundary m=3 has no fixed energy-2 sector.

originality.rationale: The exact same two-token friendship graph was previously studied for its full Laplacian spectrum and tree complexity (published-finding corpus c081d2602b88), but no complete adjacency/Hamiltonian factorization or three-sector flat-state limit was stated in its full proof. The graph is nonregular (degrees 2,4,2m), so knowing Laplacian eigenvalues does not imply hopping adjacency eigenvalues. Audenaert et al. establish the general symmetric-square Hamiltonian, not its friendship spectrum; a full comparison with published source texts and accessible claim records found no equivalent or stronger coverage. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The friendship family is a canonical collection of coupled triangular cells, and the two-excitation hard-core quantum spectrum is not reducible to the one-particle spectrum or the known Laplacian eigenvalues. The theorem supplies a complete closed spectral classification for infinitely many finite networks, identifies three explicit compact localized mechanisms, and proves a universal 1:2:1 macroscopic level-counting limit. These are physically interpretable degeneracy and localization facts, not a routine isolated numerical census.
